Hot afternoon, cool night, better wine. Verde Valley vineyards sit below 3,900 ft and can swing 30°F or more between day and dark, part of why Rhône-style grapes like Syrah and Grenache work here. The region earned official AVA status in 2021. Which would you pour first, Syrah or Grenache? Tag the friend who'd pick wrong. 🍷

Slide Rock isn't a theme park. It's Oak Creek carving its own slide through red sandstone, just a short drive north of Sedona on Highway 89A.

October brings cooler mornings and fall color to the canyon, which makes it a lovely first stop before an afternoon of Verde Valley tasting.

Canyon morning, vineyard afternoon, or both? Tell us your perfect Sedona day.

Plot twist: one of Sedona's prettiest strolls is a shopping village built on a former sycamore grove. 🍷 Tlaquepaque opened in 1973 right along Oak Creek and borrows its name from a traditional Mexican arts community. Wander the courtyards, then toast the afternoon with a tasting. Who's your stroll-and-sip partner? Tag them!

A five-story cliff dwelling tucked into limestone above Beaver Creek. Montezuma Castle in Camp Verde was built by the Sinagua people starting around the 12th century. Early settlers wrongly credited the Aztecs, which is how it got its name. It was set aside as one of the nation's first national monuments in 1906.
